summary: This paper develops a boundary-condition perspective on circuit QED dispersive readout, showing how the transmon-terminated transmission line resonator provides a frequency-dependent boundary condition whose pole structure encodes qubit transition frequencies and produces state-dependent resonator frequencies. Starting from the circuit Lagrangian and applying Sturm-Liouville theory with eigenparameter-dependent boundaries, the framework derives the dispersive shift $\chi = g^2 \alpha/[\Delta(\Delta + \alpha)]$, proves a level repulsion theorem preventing dressed modes from coinciding with transmon transitions, and extends the analysis to matched two-qubit parity measurement where engineered suppression of linear dispersive terms enables true parity-only response.
motivation: Understanding how measurement interactions select observables requires clarifying the structural role of constraints: just as Dirichlet boundary conditions in confined geometries select allowed modes by determining which states satisfy the imposed constraint, the measurement Hamiltonian $H_{\text{int}} = \hbar\chi\sigma_z\hat{n}$ selects the $\sigma_z$ basis by making its eigenstates operationally stable under environmental decoherence.
method: From the circuit Lagrangian for a transmon-terminated transmission line, the wave equation and nonlinear boundary condition at the qubit are derived via the variational principle. Linearization and quantization of the transmon via the Kubo formula yields a state-dependent boundary function $F^{(n)}(\lambda)$ with poles at transition frequencies $\omega_{nm}$; the pole-dominated approximation renders this function rational in the eigenparameter $\lambda = \omega^2/v^2$, enabling Fulton-Walter Sturm-Liouville analysis with extended Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\text{ext}} = L^2(0,L) \oplus \mathbb{C}^M$.
result: The residues are determined by matching vacuum Rabi splitting to yield $\delta_{nm} = 2Lg_{nm}^2\omega_{nm}^2/v^4$; the level repulsion theorem guarantees exactly one dressed eigenvalue between consecutive poles; multimode coupling scales as $g_n \propto \omega_n$, producing ultraviolet-divergent Lamb shifts requiring renormalization while dispersive shifts remain finite; for matched two-qubit shifts ($\chi_1 = \chi_2$), odd-parity states become frequency-degenerate but true parity measurement requires cancelling the linear term $\chi(\sigma_1^z + \sigma_2^z)\hat{n}$.
